utterances.text: Sir, if you could listen to my questions carefully, please. You actually answered my question, I think, in the first sentence of your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least if we know when he went to the Visegrad that would be great --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but perhaps that's in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, that was going to be my next question, what His Honour just asked. When was it exactly that you left for the Visegrad Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I departed Belgrade on the 18th of July 1992, and I arrived on the 19th July 1992. I'd planned to arrive on the 18th. However, communication was disrupted between Visegrad and Uzice by the Muslim forces so I could not arrive on the same day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you. Why not just answer the questions? Why say by whom you were stopped, what the weather was, whether you had had a good breakfast that day? The question simply was: When was it exactly that you left for the Visegrad Brigade. Now I saw in your statement that you said you were appointed brigade commander -- no. You first post in the VRS was that of chief of staff of the Visegrad Brigade and you had become a member on the 19th of July. Did you leave 19th of July to take up that job in the Visegrad Brigade? Yes, you arrived on the 18th. You left -- you left on the 18th, you arrived on the 19th. That was the only thing we asked you, Mr. Weber asked you. Could you please in all your next answers limit yourself to what is asked and leave out any other circumstances. If Mr. Weber is interested in it, he'll certainly ask you about it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise but I promised and solemnly declared that I shall tell the whole truth and I'm trying to abide by my words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole truth on matters that are asked. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You did not hold any positions in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps between mid-May 1992 and the 22nd of November 1994, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. I did not hold any posts in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to return to your statement that is before you. And in paragraph 3 of your statement, you reference your previous appearance in the Milosevic case. In this paragraph, you indicate that you are providing amendments or clarifications. Do I understand correctly that the rest of your statement relates to matters that were discussed with you during your previous testimony in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I did not fully understand what you are asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is the content of your statement in this case after paragraph 3 related to matters that you had previously discussed in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall what I spoke about in the Milosevic case, but I do abide by and stand by paragraph 4 and the rest of the statement. It is what I spoke on both occasions is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, it appears that your statement in the Karadzic case, which you signed on 9 December 2012, was used as a basis for the creation of your statement in the present case, the Mladic case. Am I correct in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I gave this statement on the basis of the counsel's questions, and it's almost the same as in the case of President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd now like to direct your attention to paragraphs 4 to 15 and 18 to 21 of your statement in this case. Take your time if you need to. My question is: Do I understand correctly that these paragraphs concern events leading up to the war, specifically between 1991 and early May 1992?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you ever deployed to Slovenia or Croatia as a member of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No. I was never deployed there, but I frequently visited those territories to carry out missions when I was in Kraljevo at the airforce squadron because we use the airfields and airports in those territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, please listen to my questions carefully and we will try to get this done in five hours. Do I understand correctly that paragraph 16 is a general paragraph related to the regulations that applied in the VRS between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We will return to paragraph 16 but I'd like to continue on right now to the next paragraph. Is it correct that paragraph 17 concerns your role as assistant commander for moral, religious, and legal affairs in the SRK between 22 November 1994 and 1996?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Until the end of the war. As long as the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. You still served in this position during the year 1996, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As long as Sarajevo-Romanija Corps existed, I held the post of assistant commander for morale, legal, and religious affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd now like to direct your attention to the first sentence at paragraph 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber you apparently have left the paragraphs, what was it, 4 to 15? 4 to 15. Yes. In paragraph 8, there seems to be a -- well, a translation error or a transcription error. I think in the English version it says 1992 whereas the original says 1991. Any explanation for -- Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm not the one who translates the documents, so that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but you read them as I do. I didn't translate them either. Nevertheless, I found this rather disturbing mistake. If you read it for one second in the English and if you know a tiny little bit of the history you would immediately be surprised by 1992, but I do understand that you're not -- you didn't translate. Who did translate?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based upon the footer of the document, it appears CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: CLSS. Then the CLSS should review and -- or at least the parties should carefully consider whether there are any other matters to be corrected. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Colonel, in the first sentence of paragraph 22, I would just like clarify with you that you're stating that 99 per cent of the Army of Republika Srpska were of Serb ethnicity. Is this right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to paragraph 23, this paragraph begins: "When I arrived in the SRK..." Do I understand correctly that the information you provide from paragraph 23 until the end of your statement, which is paragraph 43, relates to your time in the SRK between late November 1994 until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel, for those clarifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30897.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Colonel, in my review of the two statements, the one in this case and the one in the Karadzic case, I see that some of the wording has been changed and some of the evidence that you provided in the Karadzic Chamber was removed. It appears the first 42 paragraphs of your statements in both cases are essentially the same. Before you is an excerpt of your Karadzic statement which contains the last six paragraphs of your statement in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For the record, so the Chamber is aware, paragraph 45 of the Karadzic statement is similar to paragraph 43 in the present case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before I ask you more detailed questions about these additional paragraphs, could you please review them. And if it will assist you, I do have a hard copy present.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If the Court Officer could please hand it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Colonel, is it correct that these additional paragraphs were part of your statement in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: From which to which paragraph? Which is the first one, which is the last one? Or you mean used to be in the previous statement and now it's there? I did not understand correctly which paragraphs you enumerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, the paragraphs that I've handed to you are the additional paragraphs that appeared in your Karadzic statement which do not appear in your Mladic statement except for one of them. My question simply to you now is: Is it correct that those paragraphs were in your Karadzic statement?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. But in this statement, for today's testimony, I provided my statement on the basis of questions put to me by General Mladic's Defence counsel. In essence, they are the same. The essence of both are the same -- is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to focus on these additional paragraphs. Now, aside from paragraph 45, do these additional paragraphs relate to the taking of UN peacekeepers as hostages in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, would it be most practical if you'd just asked the witness read them again and to see whether -- he said it's all the same, he answered the questions - and apparently you were interested in this, to see whether he stands by those -- the statement in this respect? So that we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm happy to proceed. However, I do have additional questions, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay, but then at least we have a starting point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I have a reference for the use of the term "hostage"? I don't see it in the version I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I think it would have -- no, let me be clear, Mr. Weber, you used the term.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have avoided that, because it doesn't say it anywhere, then you would have avoided also this intervention which is not -- I mean, doesn't make that much of a difference on how you call things. That should be clear to you as well, Mr. Ivetic. Let's move on. Could the witness read paragraph 43 and 44 of his Karadzic statement? Could we go one page back. Witness, could you carefully read 43 -- one page back in the B/C/S original. Could you start reading at the bottom of the page and tell us when you are done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read the entire paragraph 43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are now on the next page. Could you continue to read 43 and then 44 and tell us when -- once you've done that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you stand by what is recorded in paragraph 43 and 44 of this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that these paragraphs relate to the taking of UN members as hostages in 1995?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: UNPROFOR members were captured as prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you aware that General Mladic is charged with taking UN members as hostages in this case?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I do not know that there are charges against General Mladic for taking those UNPROFOR members as hostages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before going through some additional parts of these paragraphs, I have a few questions related to your earlier testimony in the Dragomir Milosevic case. Sir, if you could just listen to me here. There is no need to look at the statement right now. At transcript page 4055 to -56 of your Milosevic testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is at 65 ter 30896, e-court pages 87 and 88.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- you were asked: "Q. Do you know anything about UN hostages? Personnel of UNPROFOR being taken hostage by the SRK forces -- by the SRK or forces of the SRK on the 26th of May 1995? At this exact time? Do you know anything about that subject?" Your answer was: "I know that there were hostages or rather that UNPROFOR members were in military terms captured, and this was done on orders by the superior command." Do you stand by this previous testimony regarding your knowledge of UN personnel being captured?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I stand by the fact that my knowledge reflects the fact that they were captured, UN UNPROFOR personnel, as -- captured as prisoners of war because in our assessment they placed themselves on the side of our enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, in the Milosevic case, at transcript page 4058, you were asked: "Q. Colonel, were the UNPROFOR hostages ever mistreated, to your knowledge, of course?" You answered: "As far as I know, they weren't. At least I don't know of any one of them being hurt. They may only have suffered some psychological consequences as a result of fear, but I have no knowledge of that." Do you stand by this testimony regarding your awareness of how the UN members were treated?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I stand by it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At transcript page 4059 in the Milosevic case, you were asked the following: "Q. Was the taking of the UN hostages consistent with the international laws of war?" You answered: "No. It was not in accordance with that." The next question: "Was there any referral made by any commander, including the corps commander of the SRK, to investigate that, the taking of UN hostages as a possible violation of the international laws of war?" You answered: "The corps commander carried out the order he received from his superior officer in relation to these activities." The next question appears interrupted, but the transcript says, "was." It appears that you continued your previous answer: "In other words, it was not him who gave this order but rather carried the order received from his superior officer." The next question: "My question again, did any commander, including the corps command of the SRK, initiate any steps to commence an investigation of the taking of the UN hostages as a possible violation of the international laws of war?" You answered: "Not that I know of." Do you stand by this testimony?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I do, but I know for a fact that there is a difference between the hostage -- the status of hostage and the status of prisoner of war. In this case, as far as I know, members of the UNPROFOR were prisoners of war and not hostages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, that is a distinction that you're making now, and I'm not looking to have a fine legal argument with you about this. What I'd like to know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I nevertheless -- it was read to you, the question that was put to you at the time: "Was the taking of the UN hostages consistent with the international laws of war?" Your answer was: "No. It was not in accordance with that."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, taking of hostages is not in keeping with it, but taking prisoners of war, that is in accordance with the international laws of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the time the question was not whether taking hostages in general is consistent with the international laws of war, but whether the taking of the UN hostages was consistent with the international laws of war. So there is this clear, and that also the context is one, in which the starting point are the facts of depriving UN persons from their liberty, as you explained in your Karadzic statement as well. So I just want to put to you that that is how one could read your statement, that it was about these events and that you'd considered them, these events, not to be consistent, not in accordance with international laws of war. I just put it to you so that you have an opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And might I point out to Your Honour, the first answer the witness on that page and the question posed on the prior page for the full context of the answer that was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that the witness didn't know everything, he heard from the media. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the prior question that that was an answer to a specific situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've seen it. It was all read to the witness, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In fact, I don't think it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That part was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What part exactly then are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's going to be transcript page 4058 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- 24 through 25, going on to page 1 -- line 1 of the last page. I don't think that part was read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see page 4058.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you for full context, Mr. Weber, read whatever Mr. Ivetic considers relevant too?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, sir, it was discussed for a while during your Milosevic testimony. Could you just tell us, the different ways in which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- I invited to you read a certain portion, Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and not to continue as if I've not asked you to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, the transcript before us reflects that you gave an answer: "I heard about that in the media but I myself didn't see anything like that. It could possibly be the case but then again it may not. I personally didn't see it." Was this your testimony in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: If you mean in relation to the term "hostages"? Is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm asking you what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't read anything here, nor do I have any insight into the overall situation, but I know that on that occasion, too, I made a distinction and I believe that I said that at the outset, the term "hostages" and the distinction between a hostage and a prisoner of war. And I believe that I said that at the beginning and I didn't feel it was necessary to reiterate it all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could have the previous page for the witness to see the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The question that was posed to you was the following: "Q. To your knowledge, were they -- were any of the hostages chained to targets, potential targets, within VRS territory? Do you have any knowledge of that?" And it was -- this was the question [sic] that you responded: "I heard about that in the media, but I'm -- I myself didn't see anything like that. It could possibly be the case but then again it may not. I personally didn't see that. Didn't see it." Is it correct that this was in reference to whether or not the hostages were chained to targets or potential targets within VRS territory?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the question that was put to me then was whether UNPROFOR members were chained to, I don't know what you said, poles or some other installations or features, and I said that I learned of something like that from the media but that I didn't know of it personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to move on unless there was another portion that you wanted me to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, at the beginning of paragraph 43, the additional paragraph 43 in the Karadzic case, you state: "I know that members of UNPROFOR were captured in the military sense and that this was done on the orders of the superior command. By superior command, I mean the VRS Main Staff." First of all, it is correct that in your position in the SRK, you were aware of the fact that UNPROFOR members were captured on the orders of the VRS Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I learned of that later at the meetings of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command, where an analysis was performed of the events preceding it, and at that meeting it was said that the order to capture UNPROFOR members had come from the Main Staff of the VRS. And here, what I said here was just a clarification of my own statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you decide not to include --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I rise to seek your guidance. At temporary transcript page 52, line 7 through 8 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please, one second. 52 you said, 7 to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Lines 7 through 8. Your Honour asked the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, one second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You asked the witness to read the entirety of 43 and 44 of this statement and asked if he stood by them. Now we are only having portions of the same read and asked for, so the record is incomplete as to what the witness stands behind. So I don't know if -- whether Mr. Weber is going to be tendering this statement or not, but I think for the record to be clear, the witness now has reviewed the entirety of those paragraphs and stands behind them but the rest of us or the record won't know what that means, what text is contained in there unless it's read into the record in its full or is admitted in written form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, one, I am planning to tender the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do that right away so that's been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Madam Registrar, the number of the excerpt of the Karadzic statement, specifically paragraph 43 and 44, would receive number?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I actually ask that paragraphs -- the remaining additional paragraphs, 43 through I believe it's 48, be admitted. I'm not going to [Overlapping speakers] questions on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the witness -- okay. Perhaps then we better wait and see whether the other paragraphs, whether the witness stands by them as well because until now we've only heard about 43 and 44.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Colonel, did you decide not to include these paragraphs in your current statement because you knew this information could be considered unfavourable to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No. I already answered that question. The questions that I was asked by the Defence counsel, I answered, and that was my statement. I didn't have before me my earlier statement in the Karadzic case. Therefore, my knowledge is the same but depending on what questions I am asked I answer them as they are asked. It wasn't me who drafted this statement. It was the result of the questions and the answers that I gave to those questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have the next page of the statement on the screen? If we could actually please go one more page in the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could just please quickly read paragraphs 46 through 48 and confirm if these paragraphs are accurate from your Karadzic statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you stand by these paragraphs from your Karadzic statement?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to go to paragraph 48. In this paragraph you refer to being shown an issue of "Srpski Borac" which you edited, and the issue contained an interview with Radovan Karadzic related to the UNPROFOR soldiers hostage but made them prisoners of war. Is it correct that "Srpski Borac" was a VRS publication that was distributed throughout the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: It isn't correct. It was a paper of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and it was primarily meant for the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps fighters. We sought, and this was one of the ways to inform the lowest levels, the privates, on the situation, so we decided to issue a paper of this nature. It was supposed to be issued even earlier but we were prevented by that because an offensive had begun, and I believe we started this in August 1995 only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, do you mean to say that it was not distributed throughout the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. On the contrary, it was meant for the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So the answer to the question was yes. The question was is it correct that "Srpski Borac" was a VRS publication that was distributed throughout the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps? And I do now understand, after having listened to seven or eight lines of your answer, that instead of what you said, the simple answer to that question is yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a paper of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, whereas VRS is a broader term. There were other corps and other units. But this paper was meant primarily for members of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was the question. That was the question. So the answer still is yes. When I'm mistaken, I'll be corrected by my colleagues. I'm open for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say it was not a VRS publication but it was distributed throughout the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. That is how I have to understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat it. This paper was issued by the organ that I led. In other words, at the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. And it was meant primarily for members of the VRS who were members of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender the additional paragraphs into evidence, they are 65 ter 30897.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30897 receives number P6644, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6644 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 03541, page 3 of the B/C/S original and page 1 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Colonel, coming up before you will be a copy of the Srpski Borac newspaper which you referred to in your Karadzic statement. The date of this issue is 2 August 1995. Directing your attention to the box on the -- which I believe is not yet up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could I please have page 3 of the B/C/S original?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the box on the left side of the page before you, is it correct that you were the publisher of this material?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The command of the Sarajevo Corps and the department that I led were the publishers of this paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You approved of what went into this publication, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the paper had its editor-in-chief. It had its various editors. And of course I had some influence over it by virtue of my function, but as this is a newspaper and the editors were journalists, they did the job as professionals, and I tried to accomplish certain objectives via texts published in this magazine that were attuned or adapted to the simple private of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you really haven't answered my question. Did you approve of what went into this publication?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No. That wasn't my task. My task was to actually get certain objectives accomplished, and that was the job of the editor-in-chief. He was in charge of the jobs that you are asking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this newspaper was published at the Lukavica barracks, at the SRK corps command?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No. That's not correct. This paper was published in Lukavica but at the faculty that was in Lukavica, because there were copying machines and machines that could produce the paper of this type and we didn't have that at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please go to the next page in the B/C/S and English versions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Colonel, on this page the interview of Radovan Karadzic begins. Before the question and answer during the interview, there is a box with a few bullet points. The last bullet point states: "Gorazde will fall even without a charge, like a ripe pear. We could have returned four cannons and avoid the crisis around Sarajevo, but we wanted to show the UN soldiers tied to the Serbian depots and warn the world what will happen to those who go against Serbs." Whose words are these? Are these the magazines or those of Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, these are the words of President Karadzic because the journalist interviewed him about the events that appear in this text. Now, whether these were his words, apparently they were, because that's what it says there, and this was done by professionals. They were journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We see that the interviewer is described or referred to as Borac. Is this a particular person or do you know who conducted this interview?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, these are technical matters that have to do with these publications. Where it says Borac, what is meant by that is the paper itself. And of course, there would always be an editor present, a journalist, and a photographer. I don't know exactly who was in this particular team who interviewed him but there were at least three members of the team present.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, it's okay if you don't know, but if you could just please tell me if you know, yes, no, in -- we can go through this rather quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The simple answer would have been, it is not a particular person. I do not know who conducted the interview, because that's the gist of your answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 7 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On this page of the interview, it appears to be where Radovan Karadzic discusses the UN members that were captured. There is a discussion of Muslim offences which is something I will discuss with you about a little bit later. Right now I'd like to focus on the passage that states: "We did not want to avoid the crisis around Sarajevo. We could return four cannons but we did not want to do that. We did not want to allow the west to ride on the low intensity war that does not disturb their public but do exhaust the Serbs in Republika Srpska, Serbian Krajina, and ultimately the Serbs in Yugoslavia. Therefore, we have consciously resorted to the fierce military response and the crisis with POW, or hostages as they call them in the west. And that is why the images on TV were drastic. Many mothers in European metropolises started thinking why should their sons be tied up to Serbian depots and NATO bombardment targets. That brought us considerable advantage, even more so because we treated our prisoners correctly." Colonel, is it correct that the SRK's own publication actually promoted the taking of UN hostages?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's absurd. This is a statement by Mr. Karadzic, the president, and he knows why he said what he said and what his objectives were, knowing who this publication was meant for.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, sir, this is a publication which you were a publisher. Is it correct you were aware of its contents?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I keep saying that I was at my press centre, that the press centre that was part of my department was issued with certain objectives, and we told them why we wanted to publish a publication of this sort --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and as professional journalists they were much better placed to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the simple question was were you aware of its contents? All the rest is answer to questions that are not put to you. Were you aware of the contents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I don't know exactly when. It depends on how much time I had to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's a simple answer. And if Mr. Weber wants to know when, then he'll ask you. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you agree with what Radovan Karadzic stated?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't agree with the essence that you are drawing from this text, but I assume what was on President Karadzic's mind and what his objectives were and I agree with those. This was meant for the ordinary private, a member of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you believe his objectives to be?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, obviously, after the completion of a very large enemy offensive, which had -- which resulted in the victory of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and the VRS, obviously there was a degree of euphoria here and propaganda which was quite natural for this kind of publication. It is the point of the newspapers and any newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you ever express any disagreement with the capturing of UN members to your superiors?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I never expressed my dissatisfaction or objections to capturing of UNPROFOR personnel because I knew that it was allowed under international rules of law and it had become apparent for a long time that not all but some UNPROFOR personnel and their commands placed themselves at the service of NATO and by extension our enemy, and -- which was at that point ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you really saying that tying UN members to targets is in accordance with the international laws of war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have not asked that question yet, so let's first ask the question, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you saying that tying international peacekeepers to targets is in accordance with international laws of war?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I do not state, I know that this is not in keeping with international law of war. But it is only from the media that I learned that several UNPROFOR personnel were tied to lamp posts or army depots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you say I learned from the media, do you mean that you learned it from the medium you were involved in yourself, where you said journalists did interview Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Karadzic apparently referred to UNPROFOR members being tied to depots, you say, "Well, I don't know whether it happened or whether he said that." Is that your evidence? Then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw that on TV much before the first issue of that newspaper was published.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you had seen it in the media, not only you learned it but you had seen it in the media. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, TV showed such footage. I saw that on TV. Whether those were credible, truthful, whether this was so or not, I do not know. But what I do know is that I saw it on TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you know that in your -- in the publication you were involved in, it was later on referred to by -- in an interview which was taken by journalists in which the words of Mr. Karadzic are recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand the gist of your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we take a break of 20 minutes. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom? No loud speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to take you back to specifically what you said in the Milosevic case. The question put to you was the following: "Q. Was the taking of the UN hostages consistent with the international laws of war?" Your answer was: "No. It was not in accordance with that." Do you acknowledge that this is what you said in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those are my words today and in any other occasion, and including that particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a simple question. The taking of UN hostages was a violation of the international laws of war as you stated in the Milosevic case, "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The term "hostage" and "hostage-taking" constitutes a violation of international of laws of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, you've tried to conflate today the notion of prisoners of war with the notion of hostage taking of international peacekeepers. With respect to prisoners of war, it is also a violation of international law to tie them to military targets, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Prisoners of war or taking members of UNPROFOR as prisoners did not run counter to international laws of war, whereas taking of hostages is a violation of international laws of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, that wasn't my question. It's a violation of international law, isn't it, to tie prisoners of war to military targets?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: All prisoners of war, whoever they belong to, if used as hostages, that contravenes international laws of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just seek clarification of that answer. Do you mean that if you tie a prisoner of war to a military target, that you use him as a hostage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know what you mean by military target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A military depot. Let's keep it very practical.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already provided an answer to that. I do believe that this contravenes international laws of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd now like to return to the interview of Radovan Karadzic that we have been looking at. Could the Prosecution please have page 5 of the B/C/S and page 4 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to go through that few other passages of this interview with you, and then I will have a question. At the end of Mr. Karadzic's answer at the top of the page of the right column before you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this is at the top of the page in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- he states: "In one more favourable for Muslims option we would accept reconstruction of the city in two entities, in two regimes. In the event that they do not accept that, we will be forced to take the entire Sarajevo just like the Jews took the entire Jerusalem." Before I go to move on to the next part of the interview, can you confirm that you see this passage?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the next page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the second paragraph in the left column, this is just below the middle of the page in the translation, in this paragraph, Karadzic states: "We need every inch in Serbian Sarajevo. We even claim rights on the centre of Sarajevo, say, the entire left bank of Miljacka river." Do you see this passage before we move on to the next one?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I can't see that paragraph. Something completely different is being shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you see the question on this page that starts: "One of the six goals of our state is the city of Sarajevo"?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I can see that, but it is not legible below.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can assist, it's -- on the left hand column, it's the part that's in bold approximately at three-quarters of the page, correct, where the pointer is now. That is the question that Mr. Weber has just referenced. The prior question relates to the area that is not as legible and it goes on to the next column.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry I had the wrong column. If we could --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention, then, to the part of the answer to this question, which I believe is in the right-hand column, the one that says: "We need every inch in Serbian Sarajevo. We even claim rights on the centre of Sarajevo, say, the entire left bank of the Miljacka River." Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we perhaps zoom in a bit on there? That's a little bit -- yes, there. You see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the next page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe this is in the bottom part of the right-hand column, in the B/C/S version, which is toward the bottom of the page of the translation. Do you see the section that states: "We won't remove our capital anywhere from Sarajevo, and if Muslims do not have the sense to give us the left bank of the Miljacka with surrounding municipalities that we control now, then I believe it will be similar with Sarajevo. Muslims will disturb us from their part of the town and we will eventually seize it entirely." Do you see this part?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: There is no such text in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you see the -- the phrase, "To keep every street"? Which I believe is in bold.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And below that, do you then see --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- what I referred to? Do you see what I referred to?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read it. I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 41 of your statement in this case, which is admitted as D554, you state the following: "I have never heard of any VRS plans to take any part of the city that was under BH Army control, and certainly not by laying siege to it." We have just looked at some statements from the Supreme Commander of the VRS, Radovan Karadzic, which were contained in the SRK's own publication. In these statements it appears he discussed dividing Sarajevo in two and if the Muslims do not agree, taking the entire city. My question: Is it correct that your statement in this case is not entirely accurate because you did hear of plans to divide the city of Sarajevo and take the city in its entirety if the forces opposing you did not agree with this division?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Now, of course I stand by what I stated in my statement because this here goes about orders of the VRS, and this is a newspaper article which serves no other purpose but to inform the public, and this is the context in which it has to be viewed. Or to achieve certain results concerning the situation on the ground, because at that time there were talks about agreements, divisions, from the very beginning, during the war, and at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, first of all, the answer that you just gave isn't accurate, is it? You said that this publication, its purpose was to inform members of the SRK at the lower ranks, not the public; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, not public but members of the corps. But in that period there was talk about exchange of territories, Ilijas for Gorazde specifically, et cetera, which led to confusion, and this is why I -- this question was asked, and president knows why he provided exactly the answer he provided. But I do stand by what I stated in my statement, and I do believe that this is -- and I think this is accurate and true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, Radovan Karadzic was the Supreme Commander of the VRS, and he's saying this in a publication that was to be distributed to the SRK. I put it to you that his words are inconsistent with what you said in your statement.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I did not consult with the president when I made -- provided my statements. I stand by my statement. It is true that I never saw personally any order whereby plans of the VRS would be detailed out with the aim of capturing Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that your -- that this publication, something that you published, is inconsistent with your own statement in this respect.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, my statement is my statement. This statement is by the president of the Republic of Srpska. He knows why he issued such a statement, and I know why I issued my statement and I stand by it. I cannot apply censorship to what president of the republic as Supreme Commander of the armed forces of Republika Srpska did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Fluegge has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just for my personal clarification, your words are, I quote: "I have never heard of any VRS plans." This is not in relation to any orders but plans. This is slightly different. Mr. Karadzic was the Supreme Commander of the VRS, and if he is telling the soldiers of the SRK what he wants to do, is that not a VRS plan? And if you say you have never heard of it, it means -- and this is really different. You never heard of it. Didn't you read it at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I probably read this, but I still maintain it is a completely different thing to have a specific concrete plan of a VRS and another thing is giving a statement to a publication, a newspaper. This is how I see things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender 65 ter 03541 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03541 receives number P6645, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6645 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Colonel, I'm now going to try to get through a couple shorter matters before the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P2185.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Appearing before you are the 1988 JNA regulations on the application of international laws of war. These regulations were previously shown to you during your Milosevic testimony. During your previous testimony, at transcript page 3972, you were asked the following question: "Q. Sir, these are regulations from the JNA from 1988 on the application of international laws of war in the armed forces of the SFRY. Did these rules continue to apply when the VRS was formed in May of 1992 and when you were a member of the VRS? Did these rules continue to apply?" You answered: "As far as I can remember, yes."

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: My answer today is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P2184 for the witness, page 2 of the B/C/S original and page 1 of the English translation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the order on the application of the rules of international laws of war in the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was also shown to you previously in the Milosevic case. This order is from the SR BiH Official Gazette and according to the end of the order, it became effective on the date of its publication, which was on 13 June 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May? Not May?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the order is dated 13 May 1992 but I believe the effective date would be the -- according to the text, the date of its publication.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to paragraph 2, which indicates that commanders of all units are responsible for the application of international rules of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could zoom out, please. And have the next page in -- page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I want to focus on the part that states: "It is the duty of the competent superior officer to initiate proceedings for legal sanctions against individuals who violate the rules of the international law of war." Is it correct that this order was in place during the entire time that you were a commanding officer in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I assumed duty in the VRS on the 19th of July 1992 and this was enacted on the 13th of May 1992. Yes -- in other words, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this order, is it correct that all officers were obligated to initiate proceedings in the event of a violation of the international laws of war?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I think you said all commanders but I can't follow everything. You said all commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question: According to this order, is it correct that all officers were obligated to initiate proceedings in the event of a violation of the international laws of war?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: All officers were duty-bound to report such cases of violation of international laws of war, whereas proceedings were initiated by those who are authorised to do so, to process such received reports, forward it to the competent organs, first of all Prosecution service, and also to report to superior officers about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So a simple answer to my question would have been "yes," right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you left out in your quote superior officers and that may create a problem because --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at -- the witness in the -- at the very end -- yes, "competent superior officers." That's what it reads. So therefore if you change it, then don't be surprised that the witness dwells upon --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So is it correct that all competent superior officers would have been required to initiate -- would be duty-bound to initiate proceedings, competent superior officers, for example, being the commanders, the deputy commanders, and members of their staffs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I've already said they were obligated to report such instances to their superior officer. In other words that should reach the level where it could be explained and then forwarded for proceedings. Now if you consider that that is initiating proceedings, then the answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This obligation applied to you during your time as the chief of staff and then brigade commander of an infantry brigade, as the chief of staff of tactical group Visegrad, and lastly when you were an assistant commander at the corps level of the SRK, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that despite regulations on the application of international laws of war in the VRS, that members of the VRS did not follow them? One example would be the taking of hostages, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object. Compound question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please split it up, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Despite there being regulations regarding the application of the international laws of war in the VRS, is it correct that members of the VRS did not follow them with one example being the taking of UN hostages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you are just repeating the question, Mr. Weber. That's not splitting it up, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Despite regulations on the application of the international laws of war in the VRS, is it correct that members of the VRS did not follow them?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, a question phrased in those terms doesn't make any sense. Now, you're putting all VRS members at the same level. There were probably some members of the VRS who did not abide by this, whether that was because of ignorance or for some other reasons I wouldn't know. However, in most cases, and for the most part, the VRS actually honoured the rules of the international law and that is a fact, and that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, one example of a violation of international laws of war would have been the Main Staff when they ordered the taking of UN hostages, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I've never heard or seen any instance where anyone from the Main Staff of the VRS ordered that UNPROFOR members be taken as hostages. However, I did hear - and I've already said this - that there was an order for UNPROFOR members to be taken prisoner and disarmed. However, the security organs were obligated to prepare those men in -- to tell them that this was just for -- as a measure of prevention in order to protect our civilians and our fighters from NATO bombing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stop you there because you're repeating what is already in your statement. Mr. Weber, it doesn't harm the Prosecution if it listened carefully to the answers to the questions and then take that into consideration when formulating a new question rather than to read it from what you have prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We have asked this enough. I'm going to move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to now discuss your assignment and duties as an assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs in the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. In this assignment, is it correct that you were directly subordinate to Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was directly the assistant commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. General Dragomir Milosevic's subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you are not a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You had a military education and did not have any training in legal matters, right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's not right. Already as cadets in military schools, we underwent training that had to do with certain legal issues. And throughout my military career, we received more and more knowledge in this field. However, at the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, in my department, there was a lawyer who dealt with technical matters that had to do with law.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you also had an assistant by the name of Captain Novak Bajic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. My assistant for legal affairs was Captain Milenko Kuzmanovic at the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Captain Novak Bajic was part of your sector?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite certain, but I think that he was an assistant for morale at the Ilijas Brigade. I'm not certain precisely what function he performed, but I am pretty sure that he was in the morale section.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you would provide written information and issue work guidelines to subordinates within your sector of the SRK command?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I provided both information and guidelines to subordinate units, at the corps commands. In other words, from brigade level down. However, in the military sense I was not their superior but, rather, it was in the technical or professional aspect. I was charged with subordinate organs that dealt with morale and legal affairs, but I wasn't their immediate superior. I was only an immediate superior to the members of my department within the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you issue work guidelines to the members of your department within the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Of course, I issued both guidelines and orders to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that part of your task in the SRK command was to strengthen the combat morale of soldiers and officers in order to build up their own beliefs?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: It is correct that I was responsible primarily for activities that had to do with the build-up of combat morale within the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. In other words, I was the top officer dealing with those matters within the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us how often you interacted with General Gvero of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Not very frequently, because we weren't on those terms but of course he was my superior officer by function. In other words, on the issues relating to morale, religion, and legal affairs, and of course I reported to him and I received certain guidelines or information from him that I then forwarded on, as instructed. Or if he left some room for me to amend those, then I did that too. Of course, it all depended on the instructions I received from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that General Milosevic abided by the decisions of the VRS Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that General Milosevic never took any actions or decisions that went outside the lines of what was ordered by the VRS Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he never issued an order that was in contravention of orders from the superior command. I've never seen an order of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30926 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Colonel, before you are VRS Main Staff sector for moral guidance, religious, and legal affairs directions and some currents issues regarding public information. The directions are dated 19 November 1994 and they are addressed to the assistant commanders for moral guidance, religious, and legal affairs including the assistant commander in the SRK. Is it correct that these directions would have applied to you?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as you could notice, I arrived at the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command after this date. This was -- this is dated 19 November 1994. I don't know. Perhaps if I read this and familiarised myself with the content, perhaps I could help, but at the time, I hadn't been at the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps; in other words, I hadn't assumed the duties -- the duty of assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I understand that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can break whenever you want. Is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's an offer I cannot resist, Mr. Weber. Mr. Dragicevic, we will adjourn for the day and we would like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.30, in this same courtroom. Before you leave this courtroom, I instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given today or whether it's testimony still to be given in the days to follow. If that's clear to you, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's clear, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 9th of July, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of July, 2014, at 9.30 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.16 p.m.,
